The backrest (rows 4-13, width 10) is a face-on panel with a light-to-dark gradient. It reads as a thin backrest rather than a missing top, so I counted it as acceptable. styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small navy office chair with about 4 blue steps (highlight on the backrest and seat edge, mid blue, dark blue, deep navy) and a grey base and wheels. Its dark edge pixels are only 6% neutral, so the outline is a navy tint of the adjacent material, not a black sticker line. That matches prop-hedge (0% neutral) and is better than prop-lamp-crook (100%). Flat-fill coverage is 0%, with no 5x5 block of one colour. It has a median of 9 colours per tile, close to prop-hedge's 10, and 12 distinct colours against 11 for the hedge and 14 for the bench. It is below the richer stall (40 colours) and well (38 colours), which are larger and more complex pieces. For a small single-material furniture piece it has comparable structure, though its ramps are slightly shallower and its texture is limited to a few seat and backrest highlight dots. A careful artist would accept it next to the bench and hedge without it looking noticeably flatter.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small blue office chair seen from the front, with a dark navy outline that leans blue rather than neutral; the measured near-neutral share of dark edge pixels is only 6%, which agrees with that. Shading is about 4 blue steps: a highlight on the backrest and seat, a mid tone, a dark tone and a deep tone, plus a grey base and wheels. The References use 5-6 steps. Flat-fill coverage is 0%, so there are no big flat areas, and the backrest and seat carry some panel and cushion variation. Median colours per tile is 9, close to the hedge's 10 but well below the stall's 17 and the well's 20. Total colours is 12 against 38-40 for the richer references, which is a similar range to the bench, hedge and lamp. The chair is a small single-tile-sized prop, so I judge density mostly by eye. It is clean and consistent, but a little simpler and thinner than the richer references, with a modest ramp and little grain on the fabric. Not sticker-like given the tinted outline, but not fully at the Beodeul level either. A careful artist would probably accept it next to the bench and hedge, though it is lower than the stall and well.
